recent_posts.title: How to share design work with clients and teams · Sketch Blog
recent_posts.summary: Sketch's Previews feature lets designers share specific slices of a document — selected pages, prototype flows, or single routes — without exposing the entire workspace. Previews are accessible via browser link with no account required, and can be protected with passwords or expiration dates. Permissions can be scoped to allow inspection and asset export for developers, or commenting for account holders. Workspace admins get a centralized view of all shared previews. Integrations with Slack (link unfurling) and oEmbed-compatible tools like Notion and Miro allow interactive inline previews, keeping design context where team conversations already happen.

recent_posts.title: Five practical ways to use Sketch's MCP server with AI clients
recent_posts.summary: Sketch's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server enables AI clients like Claude Code to automate tedious design tasks directly in Sketch documents. Five practical use cases include: swapping dark/light theme symbols automatically, replacing placeholder text with realistic data in mockups, organizing documents with consistent naming and layouts, generating color palettes from images and converting them to variables, and recreating existing websites as Sketch files by extracting styles from codebases. The server runs locally on Mac, giving designers control over document access while automating repetitive work like symbol swapping, layer organization, and style creation. Tips for effective use include being specific with prompts, using image verification tools, breaking complex tasks into steps, and always reviewing AI-generated work before sharing.

recent_posts.title: Sketch design tool features and capabilities in 2026
recent_posts.summary: Sketch highlights nine key features for 2026: a redesigned macOS editor with moveable Inspector panels, modern UI design features like stacks and frames, unique tools like minimap and command bar, flexible offline and collaborative workflows, MCP server integration for AI clients like Claude, link-based sharing with browser viewing, free developer handoff tools and commenting, team Workspace with custom folder organization, and a 30-day free trial. The tool emphasizes designer-focused features, privacy controls, and no additional costs for developers or external collaborators.

recent_posts.title: Sketch in 2025: Stacks, Glass & a macOS Tahoe Redesign
recent_posts.summary: Sketch shipped three major releases in 2025: Athens introduced Stacks (auto layout system) and Frames/Graphics (new container types replacing Artboards); Barcelona added glass effects, progressive blurs, and fade effects for iOS/macOS 26 design; Copenhagen brought a complete UI redesign for macOS Tahoe with focus mode, rewritten Inspector, stack wrapping, and one-click background removal. Additional updates include infinite folder nesting in Workspaces, a local-only MCP server for AI integration, enhanced Command Bar with component insertion, and a new Private Cloud offering for enterprise teams.

recent_posts.title: A guided tour of Sketch Copenhagen — exploring an all-new UI design · Sketch Blog
recent_posts.summary: Sketch Copenhagen introduces a major UI redesign aligned with macOS Tahoe's design language. Key updates include custom fixed sidebars instead of floating panels, document tabs moved to the sidebar, a new focus mode for the layer list, a context-aware toolbar, and a completely rewritten Inspector with movable panels replacing popovers. The color panel now features dedicated Color Variables sections, improved gradient controls, and better blend mode access. Additional improvements include 700+ new icons, enhanced Symbol overrides, custom scrubbing controls, and the ability to copy individual page and frame links for web sharing.

recent_posts.title: How Ben McCarthy is bringing Obscura’s vision to photo editing
recent_posts.summary: Ben McCarthy discusses the development of Obscura Studio, a minimalist photo editing app built entirely in Sketch. The interview covers his design philosophy of simplicity, the technical challenges of fitting editing controls into limited screen space, and how Apple's Lock Screen Camera extension influenced the app's architecture. McCarthy shares insights on iterating quickly in Sketch, balancing system components with custom controls, and his approach to product design after a decade of indie iOS development.

recent_posts.title: Frames and Graphics: A not-so-short guide
recent_posts.summary: Sketch has introduced Frames and Graphics in its Athens release, significantly changing the design workflow by replacing Artboards. Frames are optimized for interface design, featuring nestable containers with styling and layout capabilities, while Graphics serve as containers for icons and illustrations, focusing on proportional resizing without layout properties. The release encourages adoption of new practices like Auto Pin and highlights the use of Stacks for layout efficiency.

recent_posts.title: Stacks: rethinking layout in Sketch
recent_posts.summary: Sketch has introduced Stack Layouts, a new feature that allows designers to create dynamic and flexible UI elements that adapt based on their content and context. Unlike previous tools like Smart Layout, Stacks provide greater control and predictability, enabling efficient design iteration and reducing manual adjustments. Stacks can handle complex nested layouts and improve design handoff processes with developers.

recent_posts.title: A new chapter for the Command Bar
recent_posts.summary: Sketch's latest Athens release enhances the functionality of the Command Bar, enabling users to insert and replace Components more efficiently. The update also includes smarter previews, improved navigation of Libraries, and a redesigned interface for quick access to features. The enhancements aim to streamline the workflow and improve daily usage for Sketch users.

recent_posts.title: Everything we shipped at Sketch in 2024 — and what’s next
recent_posts.summary: Highlights of the new features released by Sketch in 2024 include significant improvements to their prototyping tools with Smart Animate, the introduction of the Command Bar for quicker access to actions, and a UI refresh for the web app. Looking ahead to 2025, Sketch plans to introduce an auto layout/flexbox-like feature and further enhance existing tools like Command Bar.
